product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports

Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681h)
reply: Dear Consumer, thank you for contacting us about your consumer report. We understand you disputed information on your report, including a general liability (GL) claim that you say was not paid but was reported as an inquiry coded as CO for compensation, and simple typographical errors. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681i, we are reviewing your dispute and will complete a reinvestigation, generally within 30 days of receiving your dispute, and will notify you of the results and any corrections in writing. We also understand you were asked for identifying information, including your full Social Security number and driver's license, before your dispute could be processed. We only need enough information to confirm your identity and locate your file, and we will tell you exactly what is needed. Please do not send your full Social Security number by email. Use our secure upload or call the number on your correspondence so we can verify your identity safely. We are sorry for the frustration this process has caused, and a specialist will follow up with you directly.

product: Credit reporting or other personal consumer reports
issue: Incorrect information on your report
regulations_cited: Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681c-2 (blocking of information resulting from identity theft)
Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681i (dispute reinvestigation)
Fair Credit Reporting Act, 15 U.S.C. 1681s-2 (furnisher responsibilities)
reply: Dear Consumer, we are sorry you have had to contact us several times about this. We understand you are reporting identity theft and asking us to block information on your credit report that resulted from fraud. Under Section 605B of the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681c-2), we can block identified information that resulted from identity theft once we receive the required documents. To proceed, please send us: (1) an identity theft report, such as a report filed with the FTC at IdentityTheft.gov or a police report; (2) proof of your identity, such as a government-issued photo ID and proof of address; (3) a list of each item on your credit report you believe is fraudulent, including the creditor or company name, account number (last four digits are fine), and the date it was opened; and (4) a brief statement that the items did not result from any transaction you made or authorized. Once we receive these, we will review your request, and if it is approved we will block the items and notify the company that furnished the information. We will also let you know the outcome in writing. You may also dispute any inaccurate item directly with us under Section 611 of the FCRA. Please reply with the documents or call us if you have questions. Sincerely, Complaints Team

issue: Problem caused by your funds being low
regulations_cited: Electronic Fund Transfer Act (15 U.S.C. 1693 et seq.)
Regulation E (12 CFR 1005.17) - overdraft opt-in requirements for ATM and one-time debit card transactions
Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681s-2) - furnisher accuracy duties
Regulation V (12 CFR 1022)
reply: Dear Consumer, thank you for contacting us. We understand that overdraft fees were charged to your checking account on XXXX and XX/XX/XXXX after you had opted out of overdraft coverage, and that you did not receive notice before or after these overdrafts. We also understand that the overdrafts were later reported on your credit report and that you were unable to reach the bank by phone. We are sorry for the distress this has caused. Your complaint has been escalated for a detailed review of your account records, your overdraft opt-out status and the timing of each transaction. Under Regulation E, overdraft fees on ATM and one-time debit card transactions may only be charged if you affirmatively opted in to overdraft coverage, and we will confirm whether that requirement was met. If we find that fees were charged in error, we will refund them to your account. We will also review the credit reporting of this account and correct any inaccurate information we furnished to the credit bureaus, as required by the Fair Credit Reporting Act. Our records list BMO Harris Bank N.A. as the institution on this account, while your complaint refers to Bank of the West. Please reply with your account details or any statements you have so we can confirm the correct institution and account. A member of our team will contact you with the outcome of the review. Sincerely, Complaints Team

issue: Problem with a lender or other company charging your account

reply: Dear Customer, we are sorry for the distress this situation has caused you and your family. We understand you report that a debit from your checking account was fraudulent, that it resulted from a scam, and that you notified us about it. Because you describe an unauthorized electronic transfer, your complaint will be reviewed under the Electronic Fund Transfer Act and Regulation E error resolution procedures. A specialist will investigate the disputed debit, review the records you provided, and respond to you in writing with the results. If we find the debit was unauthorized, we will correct your account, which may include a credit of the disputed amount. You may also request a copy of the documents we relied on in our investigation. Please keep all records, messages, and proof of the scam available. If you are not satisfied with our response, you may contact the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at consumerfinance.gov/complaint or the Minnesota Attorney General's Office. You may also wish to consult an attorney about your legal options. Sincerely, Bank of America Complaints Team

issue: Written notification about debt
regulations_cited: Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692e (false or misleading representations)
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692g (validation of debts)
Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, 15 U.S.C. 1692f (unfair practices)
North Carolina Debt Collection Act, N.C. Gen. Stat. 75-50 et seq.
reply: Thank you for contacting us about the letter you received from Linebarger Goggan Blair & Sampson LLP regarding a $50.00 toll charge. We understand your concern that the letter did not clearly identify who the creditor is, how the balance was calculated, or where payment should go. We have referred your complaint for review. Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (15 U.S.C. 1692g), you have the right to request written verification of the debt from the collector within 30 days of receiving the initial notice, and the collector must stop collection until it provides that verification. You may also dispute the debt in writing, and you may ask the collector to identify the original creditor. Under 15 U.S.C. 1692e and 1692f, a collector may not use false, misleading, or unfair means to collect a debt, and North Carolina's Debt Collection Act provides similar protections. Before paying, we recommend confirming the amount and the payee directly with the toll authority, as you have already done. You may also file a complaint with the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at consumerfinance.gov/complaint or with the North Carolina Attorney General's Consumer Protection Division. We will follow up once our review is complete.

We are also checking how this payment will be reported to the credit bureaus. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, we must report accurate information, and if our review shows the payment was timely or the due date was set incorrectly, we will correct your account and ask that any inaccurate late payment be removed from your credit report. A member of our team will contact you with the results. You can also reach us through our secure online messaging system, which may respond faster than the phone line. Thank you for your patience.

issue: Problem with a company's investigation into an existing problem

reply: Dear Consumer, thank you for contacting us. We understand you received a summons for a balance of over $12,000 on a Discover credit card account that you say you never opened, and that you believe you are the victim of identity theft. We are sorry for the frustration of being directed between Discover, the third-party agency, and the credit bureau without a clear resolution. Your complaint has been escalated to our fraud and dispute review team, which will coordinate the investigation of your fraud claim with the third-party agency so you do not have to repeat your account of events to each party. Because you are disputing a legal action, please do not ignore the summons. Respond to it or consult an attorney before the deadline stated in the court papers, and keep copies of everything you have sent. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act, you may request that the disputed account information be blocked from your credit reports if you submit an identity theft report, which you can create at IdentityTheft.gov (the FTC site). Under the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act, you may also request written validation of the debt, and collection activity should be paused while the dispute is open. Under the Fair Credit Billing Act, you may dispute charges on a credit card account in writing, and we will review that dispute. We will contact you once the review is complete. If you have questions in the meantime, please reply to this message and include your reference number.

issue: Problem with a purchase shown on your statement
regulations_cited: Fair Credit Billing Act (15 U.S.C. 1666)
Regulation Z billing error procedures (12 CFR 1026.13)
Fair Credit Reporting Act identity theft provisions (15 U.S.C. 1681g(e) and 1681c-2)
reply: Dear Customer, thank you for contacting us about the $9,200.00 charge on your Home Depot account dated XX/XX/2023. We understand how stressful this is, and we take your claim of unauthorized use seriously. Our investigation concluded that the information reviewed did not substantiate the claim, but we agree that you are entitled to a clearer explanation. A specialist will review your case and send you a written summary of the findings and the basis for them. Please do not send copies of your driver's license or other personal documents by mail, fax, or email to the phone number or address you were given. Instead, we will tell you through a secure channel exactly what documentation we need, and you can upload it through our secure portal or deliver it in person at a branch. Because you dispute this charge as a billing error, the Fair Credit Billing Act and Regulation Z protect your right to dispute it in writing. You may send a written notice of the billing error to the billing-error address on your statement. We must acknowledge it, complete our investigation, and either correct the account or explain why we believe the amount is correct, generally within two billing cycles and no more than 90 days. While the disputed amount is under investigation, we cannot report it as delinquent. If you believe this is identity theft, you may also file an identity theft report with the FTC at IdentityTheft.gov and request that the fraudulent information be blocked from your credit reports. Your concerns about the Account Lookup Feature, the verification used for the transaction, and the security of your online login are being forwarded to our fraud and security teams for review. You may also contact the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at consumerfinance.gov/complaint or your Massachusetts Attorney General's office at any time. Sincerely, Citibank Complaints Team

issue: Closing on a mortgage
regulations_cited: Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z), 12 CFR 1026.19 (Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure timing and revised disclosures)
Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (Regulation X), 12 CFR 1024.7 (Closing Disclosure)
Truth in Lending Act, 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.
reply: Dear Customer, thank you for contacting us about your mortgage closing. We understand this is urgent and that your closing date is approaching. We have escalated your complaint to a senior mortgage specialist who will review the Relationship Discount, the loan documents that were sent to your fianc, and the terms that were agreed. Please do not sign any further documents until you receive written confirmation of the corrected loan terms. We will work to confirm the interest rate and terms that reflect the Relationship Discount you qualified for and to issue corrected loan documents if needed. If the corrected terms change the annual percentage rate or other disclosed costs, federal rules under the Truth in Lending Act (Regulation Z) may require revised disclosures and a new waiting period before closing, and the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (Regulation X) also governs your Closing Disclosure. Please send us copies of the documents your fianc signed and any written communications about the discount, and tell us your scheduled closing date so we can prioritize your case. We will contact you shortly with an update.

reply: Dear Consumer, thank you for contacting us about the foreclosure matter on your mortgage. We understand that a foreclosure sale has been scheduled and that you believe you did not receive notice of a hearing, and that an affidavit you sent did not receive a response. product: Money transfer, virtual currency, or money service
issue: Fraud or scam
regulations_cited: N.Y. UCC Article 4-A (Funds Transfers)
reply: Dear Consumer, we are sorry about the wire transfer you sent after your email account was hijacked and the recipient bank information was changed. We understand how stressful this is. Your complaint has been referred to our fraud investigation team for review. Domestic wire transfers are governed by Article 4-A of the New York Uniform Commercial Code, which generally makes the payment order binding once it is accepted and limits the bank's liability for unauthorized or misdirected payments, so recovery depends on whether the receiving bank can return the funds. We have asked the receiving bank for the status of the return request and will contact you once we have their response. In the meantime, we recommend that you file a report with local law enforcement and with the FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (ic3.gov), secure your email account, and keep all emails and wire records related to this transaction. Please reply with any additional details or documents that may help the investigation.

Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. 6802 and 6804 (privacy and disclosure of nonpublic personal information)
Privacy Act of 1974 (applies to federal agencies, cited by consumer)
reply: Thank you for contacting us. We have received your dispute about the charge-off on your credit report, including the incorrect closing date and date of charge-off and other inaccuracies. Under the Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. 1681i), we will investigate by contacting the company that furnished the information, generally within 30 days. If the information cannot be verified as accurate, it will be corrected or deleted from your report. Please send any supporting documents and identify each inaccurate item. Regarding your privacy concerns: the Privacy Act of 1974 applies to federal government agencies, not private companies. The Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (15 U.S.C. 6802 and 6804) governs how financial institutions share nonpublic personal information, and the FCRA permits the reporting of accurate account information to consumer reporting agencies, so an opt-out may not apply to this charge-off. Because you mention accounts you do not recognize, we also recommend filing an identity theft report at IdentityTheft.gov, placing a fraud alert or security freeze on your file, and reviewing your reports from all three bureaus. You may also contact the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau at consumerfinance.gov/complaint or the California Department of Financial Protection and Innovation. This response is general information and not legal advice.

We appreciate your patience while we complete this review.
